text:
Maine's aphorism is often misread as a universal law of inevitable progress toward contract, when he meant it as a limited historical generalization about the observed shift in early legal systems from status-based to contract-based relations. It is also misunderstood as celebrating contract as superior, whereas Maine was describing a descriptive trend and later warned that contract could be socially corrosive when pushed too far. A further source of confusion is that Maine's own account of status was loose and shifting, covering any social position at all, which later writers had to narrow down.
